title.narrative: Promoting Information Integrity in Ghana as part of Praia Action plan

description.narrative: The proliferation of digital technologies in West Africa and the Sahel has expanded access to information. But it has also introduced evolving risks, with the unchecked spread of false and harmful content, including misinformation, disinformation, and hate speech (MDH). Political instability; unequal access to information ecosystems and new technologies; weak infrastructure; and low digital and media and information literacy (MIL) are challenges compounded by the misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in digital spaces and the absence of strong protective frameworks, which undermine trust in public institutions and deepen societal divides. In this context, Ghana is part of the region and is not immune to the aforementioned challenges. Although there have been attempts to address the situation, these have been ad hoc and piecemeal. In September 2025, governments, national institutions, and stakeholders held a regional conference in Praia on information integrity in West Africa and the Sahel. The conference resulted in the development of the Praia Action Plan for Information Integrity in West Africa and the Sahel (2026–2036). The plan is designed to provide a coherent, inclusive and rights-based framework for strengthening the digital information ecosystem, rebuilding public trust and ensuring that no population group — particularly women and young people — is not left behind in the region's response to the growing challenges of information disorder. The plan presents a strategic roadmap for building resilient, inclusive and transparent information ecosystems across West Africa and the Sahel.
